faq.question: What information do you need for a quote?
faq.answer: Share the item or category, quantity, required date, artwork if available and an estimated budget. If you are unsure, start with the use case and we will shortlist options.

faq.question: Can you help if I do not have final artwork?
faq.answer: Yes. Send your logo, brand colours and idea. We can advise on artwork preparation and the print method most likely to reproduce it well.

faq.question: Do you support small orders?
faq.answer: Yes. Minimum quantities depend on the product and customisation method, so we will recommend options that work for your required volume.

faq.question: Can one order include several product types?
faq.answer: Yes. Consolidating apparel, gifts and event items through one brief is one of the main reasons clients work with MySOS.

faq.question: How long does production take?
faq.answer: Timing varies by product, quantity, artwork approval and delivery requirements. Tell us your event or launch date early so we can plan backwards.

faq.question: Can I see a sample before full production?
faq.answer: Sampling is available for suitable projects. We will explain the sample type, cost and timing during quotation.

seo.title: Ideas and Buying Guides | MySOS Blog
seo.description: Practical guides to custom printing, materials, merchandise planning and successful project delivery.

hero.heading: Make the next merchandise decision easier.
hero.body: Clear explanations, planning tips and behind-the-scenes guidance from sourcing through delivery.
hero.imageAlt: Custom products arranged as inspiration for a merchandise project

articles.title: How to choose a T-shirt printing method
articles.summary: A practical guide to silkscreen, DTF, DTG, embroidery and sublimation for common apparel briefs.
articles.imageAlt: Custom apparel showing a detailed printed design
body: Start with the fabric, artwork, quantity and how the garment will be used. Those four details narrow the options more reliably than choosing a method by name.

Silkscreen is often strong for bold designs and larger quantities. DTF supports colourful detail across many garments, while DTG suits detailed artwork on suitable cotton apparel. Embroidery adds texture and a premium feel. Sublimation is ideal when colour needs to become part of performance fabric.
You do not need to decide alone. Share the garment, artwork and order size, and MySOS can recommend the practical route.

articles.title: What to prepare before requesting a merchandise quote
articles.summary: The five details that turn a broad idea into a useful, comparable recommendation.
articles.imageAlt: A custom product being prepared as part of an order
body: A strong enquiry does not need exact product codes. It needs a clear audience, approximate quantity, required date, budget range and the action or feeling the item should support.
Send your artwork if it exists, but do not delay the conversation if it does not. A logo, brand guide or even a reference image can be enough to begin.
Mention whether items will be packed individually, distributed at an event or delivered to more than one location. Fulfilment details can affect the best recommendation.

articles.title: Choosing materials people will keep using
articles.summary: How use case, care, comfort and perceived value shape better product choices.
articles.imageAlt: Durable customised merchandise designed for regular use
body: A useful item earns repeated visibility. Think about where it will be used, how often it will be handled and what care it needs before comparing finishes.
For apparel, comfort and climate matter as much as weight. For bags, strap comfort and capacity shape real-world use. For drinkware, lid design and cleaning can matter more than an unusual shape.
The best material is the one that supports the audience and purpose without adding cost they will never notice.

articles.title: Behind the scenes of a multi-item event kit
articles.summary: How one brief becomes a coordinated set of apparel, lanyards, signage and participant gifts.
articles.imageAlt: A large event using coordinated branded materials
body: Multi-item projects work best when the visual system, quantities and delivery milestones are agreed before individual products enter production.
The process starts with the participant journey: what people wear, carry, receive and see. That creates a useful priority list and prevents low-impact items from consuming the budget.
A consolidated schedule then connects artwork approval, sampling, production and delivery so every part is ready for the same event date.
